query: driftingly/rector-laravel upstream issue #574 and Symplify contracts abandonment: compare a minimal maintained fork of the contracts package (real code/provenance/tests) against a Rector-Laravel fork removing documentation-only getRuleDefinition methods and DocumentedRuleInterface. Rector 2 official guide removed this API; Rector 2.6.7 currently bundles unprefixed Symplify\\RuleDocGenerator classes in vendor. Is relying on these bundled classes an officially supported replacement or just undocumented internals? Give maintainability recommendation for strict no-abandoned Composer audit and no fake replace. Cite primary source code and latest upstream issue comments only.

content.text:
For your strict “no abandoned packages, no fake replace” policy, I recommend a small Rector-Laravel fork that removes its documentation contract—not a fork that merely starts importing Rector’s bundled Symplify classes. A genuine maintained contracts fork is defensible and may involve fewer immediate code changes, but Rector 2 explicitly supports rules without getRuleDefinition(); that is the stronger long-term integration boundary.

## Supported API versus bundled code

The important distinction is between availability and support:
- Rector’s official upgrading guide says: “AbstractRector get focused on code, the getRuleDefinition() is no longer required.” This supports implementing transformation rules without that documentation method.
- I verified that the Rector 2.6.7 distribution contains vendor/symplify/rule-doc-generator-contracts, including its source directory, Composer metadata and licence, at distribution commit 96bb5f83520f0f41e3130cf2178cd13890a242b7. See the .
- That presence does not establish an official replacement package or a compatibility promise

Sources:
1. [github](https://github.com/rectorphp/rector-src/blob/main/UPGRADING.md)
2. [tagged bundled source](https://github.com/rectorphp/rector/tree/96bb5f83520f0f41e3130cf2178cd13890a242b7/vendor/symplify/rule-doc-generator-contracts)
